ops.body: - A ride's dashed line is sent as data while it is ridden, at most ten times a second (`REPLAY_ENGINE.resendMs`), so its tip can trail the dot by a tenth of a second and RC3's "nothing sent as time passes" does not hold during a ride: maplibre-gl 6.16 draws a dash over line metrics at a scale that follows the line's length, so a revealed ride came out as fine dots. A phone's lines are data too (`lineGradient` on MapLibre RN untried)
ops.intro: The replay's rework, built whole on its branch and shown at the preview address before any of it is deployed (the owner's "Build it whole, show me first", Nov 18). The engine is built (RC1-RC10, RC48's engine part); the look is not. Measured in headless Chromium with software GL, never on an iPhone (`docs/research/replay-frame-pipeline.md`, `scripts/perf-replay.js`).

ops.body: - MapLibre covers the tiles of about thirty mostly empty sources every frame: 4.7% of the main thread in a 4x profile of the path beat. Hiding the layers of an empty source would skip it; left because it changes every map, not only the replay's

- On a stretch React still commits three to five times a second (it was about 22): the clock's leaf at each new minute, and the map's view, which reaches React at most twice a second during the path, so the scale bar and the pins' grouping can follow a zoom half a second late. A clock whose digits are written with no render would remove the first

- The loading skeleton still pulses through `Animated`, which renders on the web: about sixty small commits a second while a memo or video loads. The fog beat still runs on a 33 ms interval that renders the screen; RC23 reworks the opening

- [owner] The ceiling on frames a second (`REPLAY_ENGINE.frameMs`, 0: every display frame) is the owner's to choose on the iPhone at the first look: a replay's link takes `?fps=30` (or any number) to try one without a build. The link parameter was not asked for and goes once the number is chosen. The test machine never exceeds 30 frames a second, so RC6 is held by the stepper's unit test alone

- Thin in the tests: RC1 is read from what the map is told (the dot, the line's end and the camera's centre written in one call before one redraw), not from pixels; RC8's rebuilt telling (a moment deleted from the viewer mid-path) is unit-tested only; RC7's journey checks cover a card, a bubble and the clock, grids and whispers only by unit tests of their poses; the seeded walk's stretches last about 0.9 s, so RC2 and RC3 are counts over that window

- The React Compiler (decision 0207) came on with a merge of `main` after the engine was built, and the stage stayed empty (no clock, no card): it read the frame from its store in a render and the compiler kept the first read. Fixed (`live.staged`, three tests under RC7). What it showed: `arch/reactCompiler.test.ts` (CM2) scans `.tsx` files only, so a hook in a `.ts` file that the compiler skips (`useCeremonyLoop.ts` disables `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` once) or miscompiles is in no list, and only a journey caught this one

argv: The replay screen still renders at the clock's 30 fps
replay ceremony RC2 (decision 0206): the screen no longer renders per frame; what is left for a device is filed under the replay ceremony in docs/NATIVE_UNVERIFIED.md

ops.body: - [ ] **Do:** watch a walk's replay (photos, a note, a memo, a video, a gap) and a day's replay to their cards. **Expect:** the walker's dot and the camera move together and smoothly; the walked line follows, its end at most a tenth of a second behind the dot; nothing else on the map flickers as it plays; at the card the whole trace is drawn with no gap or blink. (RC1, RC3, RC9)
ops.intro: The engine only (RC1-RC10): one frame loop outside the screens' rendering. On a phone the walker is a `ReplayDot`, the camera a `Camera.jumpTo` each frame, both lines data sent at most ten times a second, and the overlays' motion `setNativeProps` (`liveStyle.ts`). None of it has run on a device.

ops.body: - [ ] **Do:** in the same replays watch a card grow from its pin and tuck into the pile, a grid's cells swipe in, a note's bubble come and go, a passed place's whisper, the dim across a gap and "N min later". **Expect:** each moves smoothly and ends where it did before; none sticks at the start of its move, jumps when another overlay arrives, or appears at rest without having grown; the clock's digits roll a minute at a time with no stutter of the map under them. (RC7)

- [ ] **Do:** during a replay press Hold, tap the map, press Next twice quickly, open the pile, lock the phone for a minute and unlock, then delete a photo from the viewer. **Expect:** held, everything stands still; Next lands on the next moment and then the one after; the viewer holds the replay; a locked screen never skips to the card; after the delete the replay goes on from the same place. (RC5, RC8)

- [ ] **Do:** with Reduce Motion on, watch a replay; then watch the replay of a walk with a bus ride. **Expect:** with Reduce Motion the map stays still, the walker moves over it, cards fade in place, and it lasts as long as without it; the ride is dashed, under the walked line, and grows with the dot. (RC1, RC3, RC10)

- [ ] **Do:** on a development build set `globalThis.__perf = {}` in the console, watch a replay and read `__perf`. **Expect:** `render:replay` (or `render:day`) and `render:map` rise only when a moment arrives or leaves; note the frames a second, and whether a ceiling (`REPLAY_ENGINE.frameMs`) looks better. (RC2, RC6)
